educationalModelNote: All numerical models are simplified educational models, not specifications of a real robot.

missions.title: ENERGY VS POWER
missions.concept: Energy determines how long the robot can operate; power determines what it can do at a moment. They are related but not interchangeable.
missions.scenario: Mission average and peak loads are measured. Size usable energy and reserve policy.
missions.goalText: Provide more than one hour of planned runtime with explicit reserve.
missions.transferText: Recover runtime after average mission power rises; peak load remains a separate capability problem.

missions.title: BATTERY & BMS
missions.concept: Pack voltage, capacity, state of charge and BMS current limits jointly determine available energy and peak capability.
missions.scenario: SoC and BMS current limit are measured conditions. Choose pack voltage/capacity.
missions.goalText: Support the event while preserving mission reserve.
missions.transferText: Adapt pack operating point when low SoC reduces current headroom.

missions.title: REGENERATION & POWER FLOW
missions.concept: Regenerative braking only recovers energy that the bus/battery can accept; near full charge, returned power may need to be limited or dissipated.
missions.scenario: Regenerated power and SoC are imposed by motion/battery state. Configure charge acceptance and dump capacity.
missions.goalText: Keep returned power inside battery acceptance plus explicit dump/buffer capacity.
missions.transferText: When charge acceptance collapses, manage excess energy rather than pretending regeneration is always free.

missions.title: HEAT & COOLING
missions.concept: Thermal resistance sets steady temperature rise; cooling-path degradation reduces sustainable capability.
missions.scenario: Heat generation and inlet blockage are imposed. Tune thermal path and active cooling.
missions.goalText: Create sustainable thermal margin under the current loss.
missions.transferText: Recover continuous capability after the cooling path degrades.

missions.title: DOCKING, DERATING & SEALING
missions.concept: Energy reserve, temperature and docking availability form one mission-level decision problem.
missions.scenario: SoC, temperature and dock distance are measured. Choose transit speed and mission state.
missions.goalText: Choose return-to-dock while reserve and thermal headroom still support it.
missions.transferText: Return conservatively before sealed-operation derating becomes critical.

missions.title: ENERGY GATE
missions.concept: Demonstrate runtime, peak-current and thermal/safe-state reasoning as one coupled energy architecture.
missions.scenario: Each case imposes mission load/temperature. Size energy, bus voltage and cooling boost.
missions.goalText: Complete the three energy gate cases.

gateCases.name: RUNTIME
gateCases.text: Plan at least 90 min plus 15% energy reserve.

gateCases.name: PEAK CURRENT
gateCases.text: Keep the imposed 8 kW event below 125 A by choosing bus voltage.

gateCases.name: THERMAL / SAFE STATE
gateCases.text: Hotter mission: preserve >8°C thermal margin and >150 Wh after 90 min.
